AWARD

This appeal preferred by the Insurance Company under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of award dated 23.11.2022 passed by Learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhabua, District Jhabua (M.P.) in Claim Case No.120 of 2019 on account of exonerating the Insurance Company from the liability to pay compensation.

sentences.text:
1 2. Brief fact of the case is that on 30.08.2019 in morning at 07:00 AM, deceased Thithabai W/o Bhurji Damor was standing in front of her house on side of the road situated in Village Shujapura,
Tehsil Thandla, District Jhabua (M.P.), meanwhile the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration number MP-09 KC-7032 drive rashly and negligently and hit the deceased; due to that,
the deceased received injuries and declared dead on the spot.
3. The claimant filed a claim petition before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhabua for seeking compensation against the owner, driver and Insurance Company.
4. Respondent - Insurance Company filed its written statement and denied all the averments pleaded in the claim petition.

5. The Claims Tribunal framed issues and after taking evidence, allowed the claim petition filed by the claimant and awarded compensation of Rs.3,27,400/- (rupees three lakhs twenty seven thousand four hundred only) with interest in favour of the claimant and against the present appellant - Insurance Company as well as respondents No.2 and 3 - driver and owner of the offending vehicle.

6. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, Insurance Company filed this appeal and submitted that the Tribunal committed gross error imposing liability on the present appellant - Insurance Company, on account of the Driving Licence.

7. The appellant - Company adduced evidence before the Tribunal that on the date of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not having the effective and valid Driving Licence, but the Tribunal had not considered the appellant's evidence and committed gross error.

8. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that the appellant examined DW-1 Sajjan Singh, who was an employee of the Regional Transport Office (RTO), Ratlam and produced the record and submitted that Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) Transport Driving Licence is not issued by the Office.
So, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation and prayed for its exoneration.
9. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent - claimant supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.

10. Heard learned counsel of both the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal.
11.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective Driving Licence.
He submitted that the accident occurred on 30.08.2019 and Driving Licence was issued in favour of driver of the offending vehicle on 30.11.2019.

12. DW-1 Sajjan Singh, who was an employee of RTO, Ratlam stated in examination-in-chef that driver of the offending vehicle possess a Driving Licence of Motorcycle with Gear from 17.05.2012 to The Oriental Insurance Co. sentences.text: He stated in examination-in-chief that at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle does not possess a Driving Licence of Light Commercial Vehicle.

13. The Claims Tribunal in para 22 of the impugned award observed that in assumption that before issuing Driving Licence for driving Heavy Goods Vehicle, driver of the offending vehicle may possess a Learning Licence.

14. It is the duty of the driver of the offending vehicle to depose the evidence before the Tribunal that he has a Learning Driving Licence at the time of accident, but the driver of the offending vehicle did not adduce any evidence in this regard.
So, he is unable to adduce any evidence, that he possess a Learning Licence to driver Heavy Commercial Vehicle.
So like all this evidence, the Tribunal has committed error by holding that the driver of the offending vehicle has possess a Learning Licence at the time of accident.
So, the findings of the Tribunal in this regard are not correct in the eyes of law.

15. So, in the considered opinion of this Court, as per the aforesaid discussion, the Tribunal has committed error that the driver of the offending vehicle possess a valid and effective Driving Licence, at the time of accident.

So, the Insurance Company has proved that at the time of accident,
the driver is not a valid and effective Driving Licence.
So, the driver and owner breached the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.

16. So, on violation of terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy, the appellant - Insurance Company is not jointly and severally liable to make payment of compensation, however, in the light of judgment passed by the Apex Court in case of Amrit Pal Singh v. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited reported in 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) page 8, whereby it was held that the Insurance Company shall be liable to make payment of compensation amount to the claimant with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 17. Accordingly, award dated 23.11.2022 passed by Learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhabua, District Jhabua (M.P.) in Claim Case No.120 of 2019 is hereby modified, as indicated herein above.
18. As a result, the present miscellaneous appeal is allowed.
